cards.text: The land is being handed out tribe by tribe, and now it's the turn of the descendants of Joseph. Their share runs from the Jordan at Jericho, up into the hill country of Bethel, and west all the way to the Sea. Friend, I spent years in a drawer the size of a shoebox, and these folks get a stretch from the river to the SEA.

cards.question: This land is the inheritance of Joseph's two sons, ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then Ephraim's own borders get mapped out, clan by clan, past Upper Beth-horon, Janoah and Jericho, and west to the Brook of Kanah and the Sea. Ephraim even gets some cities set apart inside Manasseh's land, which is like keeping your stuff in your brother's garage forever.
Ephraim moves in, but Canaanites are already living in the city of Gezer. That's getting the keys to your new place and the last tenants are still on the couch holding the remote.

cards.question: So what does Ephraim do about the Canaanites living in Gezer?

answers.text: They do not drive them out
They drive every one of them out
They hand Gezer over to Manasseh

cards.question: True or false: The Canaanites stay in Gezer among the Ephraimites, but as forced laborers.

cards.text: Now it's Manasseh's turn, Joseph's firstborn son. And Manasseh's own firstborn, Machir, already received Gilead and Bashan. Firstborn of a firstborn. That man has never waited in a line in his LIFE.

cards.question: Why did Machir, Manasseh's firstborn, receive Gilead and Bashan?

answers.text: Because he was a man of war
Because his clan was the largest

cards.text: So this allotment is for the rest of Manasseh's clans: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. Six family names, and I promise, friend, there's no spelling test.
But in the line of Hepher, a man named Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. Five names, and not one son among them. So where does their share go?

cards.question: Zelophehad's daughters step up to make their case. Who do they go to?

answers.text: Eleazar and Joshua and the leaders
Caleb and the elders of Judah
Aaron and the sons of Levi

cards.question: The daughters tell them, "The LORD commanded ___ to give us an inheritance among our brothers."
True or false: Joshua turns Zelophehad's daughters away and gives their share to their uncles.

cards.text: Ten shares fall to Manasseh, plus Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan. Those daughters walked in with ONE sentence and walked out with land, and I can't even get my oven timer to listen to me.

cards.question: Why does Manasseh end up with ten shares on top of Gilead and Bashan?

answers.text: The daughters got shares among the sons
Machir won more land in battle
Ephraim gave up some of its land

cards.text: Now Manasseh's borders get mapped out, from Asher down to Michmethath near Shechem, then on to the Brook of Kanah and the Sea. Ephraim's territory sits to the south and Manasseh's to the north. Around Tappuah it gets tangled: the region is Manasseh's, but the town itself is Ephraim's, like two neighbors sharing a driveway with ONE parking spot.
Manasseh is also assigned six cities inside Issachar and Asher, including Beth-shean, Taanach and Megiddo. Big names. Big plans.

cards.question: Can Manasseh move into those cities assigned to them inside Issachar and Asher?

answers.text: No because the Canaanites are determined to stay
Yes and the Canaanites leave without a fight
No because Joshua gives those cities to Asher

cards.text: Time goes by, and the Israelites grow stronger. Then they put those Canaanites to forced labor.

cards.question: True or false: Once they're stronger, the Israelites drive the Canaanites out completely.

cards.text: Then the sons of Joseph come to Joshua, and friend, they are NOT here to say thank you. They've got a question about their share.

cards.question: What do the sons of Joseph ask Joshua about their share?

answers.text: Why they got only one portion
Why their land has no springs
Why Judah got the best hills

cards.question: The sons of Joseph say they have many people because the LORD has ___ them abundantly.

cards.text: Joshua hears them out. And he's got an answer ready, in case the hill country of Ephraim really is too small for them.

cards.question: What does Joshua tell the sons of Joseph to do if the hill country is too small?

answers.text: Go clear land in the forest
Take some of Judah's hill towns

cards.text: Joshua's answer is basically: big family? Great, here's an axe. But the sons of Joseph push back. The hill country isn't enough, they say, and the Canaanites in the valley have them worried.

cards.question: The sons of Joseph say the Canaanites in Beth-shean and the Valley of Jezreel have iron ___.

cards.text: So Joshua turns to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh. He tells them, "You have many people and great strength."

cards.question: True or false: Joshua tells the house of Joseph they won't have just one allotment.
And the strong Canaanites with their iron chariots? What does Joshua tell Ephraim and Manasseh about them?

cards.text: So the hill country is theirs too: it's a forest, clear it, and its farthest limits are theirs. Friend, that's a pep talk AND a chore list in one speech.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "The LORD commanded ___ to give us an inheritance among our brothers.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The punchline "from the river to the SEA" repeats a well-known political slogan word for word. Even if it's unintended, it brings politics into the lesson. The geography of Joshua 16:1-3 needs a different joke.

rule.text: No cursing, crude humor, innuendo, or social or political commentary.

findings.problem: The two-blank question "Joseph's two sons, ___ and ___" marks Ephraim as blank 1 and Manasseh as blank 2. The question doesn't say which order it wants, and either order is reasonable. Manasseh is the firstborn (Josh 17:1), but 16:4 names Ephraim first. A baker who puts Manasseh first would be marked wrong for a defensible pick.
findings.question: When a fill in the blank has two blanks that could reasonably go in either order, should both orders count as right, or should the question be reworded so only one order fits?

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences. A card that isn't the opening card can have at most two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke "Firstborn of a firstborn. That man has never waited in a line in his LIFE" suggests Machir got Gilead and Bashan for being firstborn. Joshua 17:1 says it was "because Machir was a man of war," and the very next card asks exactly why. The joke muddies the fact the baker is about to be asked.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.

findings.problem: The joke "there's no spelling test" is a school reference.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. The line "Five names, and not one son among them" also just repeats what the first sentence already said.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Eleazar shows up for the first time in this card's right answer, and nothing says who he is. Joshua 17:4 calls him "Eleazar the priest."

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card goes straight from "Ten shares fall to Manasseh" to "Those daughters... walked out with land." Putting the two side by side tells the baker the answer to card 15, which asks why Manasseh gets ten shares (the daughters got shares among the sons, 17:6).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The comparison "two neighbors sharing a driveway with ONE parking spot" is about sharing and competing for one thing. In Joshua 17:8 the land is split: the region around Tappuah belongs to Manasseh and the town itself belongs to Ephraim. The comparison doesn't have the same action, and it suggests a conflict the text never mentions.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the city list, "Big names." and "Big plans."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Saying the Israelites put the Canaanites to forced labor already tells the baker the Canaanites are still there. That gives away card 5, which asks whether the Israelites drove them out completely (False, 17:13).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card is a flat retelling with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences and more than two beats: the callback to the axe, the pushback, and the Canaanites in the valley.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "The Canaanites in the valley have them worried" states a feeling as fact. Joshua 17:16 only reports what they said.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.
